title: 1kg Grouper + Giant Seafood Rice | Da Nang's Secret Gem
description:
Discover one of the best hidden seafood restaurants in Da Nang as we explore a local-recommended spot just minutes from the fishing boats near Son Tra Peninsula. After a week of bad weather and illness, the sunshine finally arrives — giving us the perfect chance to hunt down fresh seafood straight from the source.

Tucked away in the back streets, Nan Danh Seafood Restaurant is a huge, mostly local seafood venue you’d never find without insider tips. With fishing boats docked nearby, this place promises some of the freshest seafood in Da Nang — and it delivers.

We order a massive fried grouper (over 1kg) topped with mango, mint, garlic, and chili, alongside a giant seafood fried rice packed with shrimp, squid, and octopus. From crispy fish skin to juicy flesh and the perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and herbal flavors, this meal turns into one of the best seafood experiences we’ve had in Vietnam.

If you’re looking for authentic Da Nang food, local seafood restaurants, hidden gems, and travel tips for Vietnam, this is a must-watch. See what it’s like to eat where the locals eat and why some of the best places aren’t on the tourist map.

In this video:

* Exploring Da Nang’s fishing coastline
* Finding a hidden local seafood restaurant
* Fresh grouper cooked Vietnamese style
* Massive seafood fried rice review

This is the final video in our Vietnam travel series, and this time we’re eating our way through Hoi An.

If you're looking for the best food in Hoi An, planning a Hoi An food tour, searching for Hoi An street food, or wondering what to eat in Hoi An Vietnam, this video shares the food and drink experiences that genuinely stood out during our trip.

We start with our main Vietnamese dinner at MẸT Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegetarian Food in Hoi An Ancient Town. The restaurant sits directly opposite the river, with its front entrance opening onto the historic streets and the back overlooking the riverside.

Instead of ordering just one dish each, we shared several Vietnamese dishes so we could try more variety and compare our reactions.

One of the most interesting local specialties we tried was White Rose, or bánh bao bánh vạc — delicate steamed dumplings known for their flower-like appearance and strong connection to Hoi An.

We also tried Vietnamese pancakes, fresh juices and other shared dishes while keeping our genuine reactions and conversations in the video.

From there, we continue exploring Hoi An’s food scene, including tropical drinks, street sweets and fresh sugarcane juice.

We also visit Chợ Hội An, where one of the most interesting parts of the local dining culture is how many small food stalls sit together in one place. Diners can sit directly along the counters while dishes are prepared in front of them, making the experience feel completely different from a normal restaurant.

Another drink that caught our attention was a popular Hoi An herbal drink with its distinctive lotus-style presentation — the kind of simple local stop that often has people lining up in the Ancient Town.

At Hoi An Night Market, we walk through food stalls, watch dishes being prepared and try a few smaller snacks rather than pretending we tasted everything on offer.

We also share one practical lesson from our trip: online menus are not always up to date, so it is worth checking the current menu and prices before ordering.

title: Hue - Where harmony endures |  VietNam Travel Documentary | Stepping into Wonder
description:
Discover **Hue Vietnam**, the former imperial capital where rivers, mountains, ancient palaces, and quiet traditions come together in remarkable harmony.

In this episode of *Stepping into Wonder*, we journey through **Hue Vietnam** beyond its famous monuments — exploring the ideas, landscapes, and centuries of history that shaped the city. Along the Perfume River, the Imperial City and the royal tombs reveal a world designed not simply to impress, but to exist in balance with nature.

🏯 Wander through the ancient Imperial City
🌿 Discover the landscape and philosophy behind Hue's royal architecture
🌊 Follow the Perfume River through the heart of the former capital
👑 Explore the legacy of the Nguyen Dynasty and its imperial tombs
🛕 Experience pagodas, gardens, traditional culture, and the quiet rhythm of local life

What makes **Hue Vietnam** extraordinary is not only what remains from the past, but the relationship between everything around it. Mountains become protective horizons. Water carries both life and memory. Architecture follows the landscape. Gardens, courtyards, gates, and temples seem to invite the natural world inside.

Once the seat of the Nguyen Dynasty, Hue was Vietnam's imperial capital from 1802 to 1945. Today, the Complex of Hue Monuments is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, preserving an exceptional chapter of Vietnamese history and culture.

Yet **Hue Vietnam** is more than an imperial story.

Beyond the citadel walls, life moves at another pace — along the river, beneath old trees, through quiet streets and places where traditions continue without needing to announce themselves. Here, history does not feel separated from everyday life. It simply remains part of it.

Through cinematic landscapes, gentle storytelling, and moments of stillness, this travel documentary invites you to experience **Hue Vietnam** slowly — not simply as a destination to visit, but as a place to feel.

✨ **Stepping into Wonder**
Slow down and rediscover the world through beautiful stories.

title: My Son Sanctuary, Vietnam | What It’s Really Like on a Rainy Day
description:
My Son Sanctuary, Vietnam | What It’s Really Like on a Rainy Day
What is My Son Sanctuary really like on a rainy day?
In this video, we visit My Son Sanctuary in Da Nang, Vietnam, on a light rainy morning and take you through the ancient temple groups, forest paths, archaeological remains, and museum.
We started from Da Nang center in the morning and arrived at My Son around 8:55 AM. From the entrance, we took the electric shuttle into the archaeological area, then continued on foot through the temple groups.
Along the way, we explored Groups B, C and D, visited Group A and Group G, passed by Group F, and came across a bomb crater that remains visible within the archaeological site. We also stopped at the museum before leaving to learn more about Champa history, temple architecture, Sanskrit inscriptions, and the conservation work carried out at My Son.
The light rain continued throughout our visit, but it didn't cause us any trouble. In fact, the cooler weather and quieter atmosphere made walking around the sanctuary very comfortable for us.
We finished our visit at around 11:15 AM, after about two hours of exploring, while other visitors were still arriving.
If you're wondering whether light rain is a reason to skip My Son Sanctuary, we hope this real experience helps you decide what to expect.
📍 My Son Sanctuary, Da Nang, Vietnam
🏛️ UNESCO World Heritage Site
🌧️ Visited on a light rainy morning

title: Da Nang Day 5 🇻🇳 | Marble Mountains, Hoi An Night Market & Lantern Boat
description:
Welcome to Vietnam Travel Vlog Day 5! In this vlog, we went on a half-day tour from Da Nang covering some of the most beautiful and cultural places in Central Vietnam—Marble Mountains and Hoi An Ancient Town ✨

We started our day by visiting the famous Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son), known for their caves, temples, viewpoints, and panoramic views. This place is a must-visit when you’re in Da Nang and gives you a perfect mix of nature, history, and spirituality 🏔️🛕

After exploring Marble Mountains, our tour package included dinner, which made the trip very convenient and hassle-free 🍽️

Later in the evening, we headed to Hoi An Ancient Town, where we explored the colorful Hoi An Night Market, enjoyed shopping, street food, and the magical evening atmosphere 🌃

The highlight of the day was the Hoi An Lantern Boat Ride on the Thu Bon River. Floating lanterns, lights, and reflections make this experience truly unforgettable and one of the most romantic things to do in Vietnam 🏮🚣‍♂️

This vlog will help you understand how to plan a Marble Mountains and Hoi An tour from Da Nang, what’s included in the package, and whether it’s worth it—especially useful if you’re planning a Vietnam trip from India.

Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary - It is a famous UNESCO World Heritage Site in Central Vietnam which showcase the ancient Champa civilization and its Hindu temples. 
These ruined Hindu temples are abandoned as of now and these Hindu temples were constructed in between the 4th and the 13th century by the Kings of Champa. Inside there is a museum too which also explains the history of this place.
There is also a dance performance done by the locals which shows how the Champa civilization used to celebrate festivals.

Han River - Han River is a major waterway that flows through the heart of Da Nang. It is famous for its vibrant city life, scenic beauty, and iconic bridges. 

Han Market - It is one of the famous and old markets of Da Nang. A wide range of goods, including fashion, souvenirs, and local specialties can be seen here. Locals and tourists both can find everything here like clothing and accessories to dried foods and unique handicrafts. 

Dragon Bridge - It is one of the famous Bridges in Han River Da Nang, which can "breathe" fire and water, adding to the city's unique charm. This is also one of the main tourist attractions at night time.

description:
🇻🇳 வியட்நாம் பயணம்: ₹15,000-ல் சுற்றிப் பார்க்க முடியுமா? | Vietnam Travel in Tamil | Vietnam Facts

வியட்நாம் உண்மையிலேயே குறைந்த செலவில் சுற்றிப் பார்க்கக்கூடிய நாடா? 🇻🇳 வெறும் ₹15,000 அல்லது ₹20,000 இருந்தால் வியட்நாம் செல்ல முடியுமா? அழகான கடற்கரைகள், பனிமலைகள், உலகப் புகழ்பெற்ற குகைகள், பழமையான கோவில்கள், French Colonial Architecture, நவீன skyscrapers, விதவிதமான உணவுகள் மற்றும் உலகப் புகழ்பெற்ற Vietnamese Coffee என ஒரே நாட்டில் இத்தனை அனுபவங்கள் எப்படி கிடைக்கிறது?

இந்த வீடியோவில் Vietnam Travel, Vietnam Tourism, Vietnam Facts in Tamil பற்றி முழுமையாக பார்க்கலாம்.

இந்தியர்களிடையே வியட்நாம் ஏன் வேகமாக பிரபலமாகி வருகிறது? 🇮🇳✈️🇻🇳
2023 மற்றும் 2024 ஆண்டுகளில் வியட்நாமுக்கு சென்ற இந்திய சுற்றுலாப் பயணிகளின் எண்ணிக்கை எப்படி அதிகரித்தது? வியட்நாம் உண்மையில் Thailand, Malaysia போன்ற நாடுகளைவிட குறைந்த செலவிலான சுற்றுலா destinationஆ? இந்த கேள்விகளுக்கான பதில்களையும் இந்த வீடியோவில் தெரிந்துகொள்ளலாம்.

இந்த பயணத்தில் நாம் பார்க்கும் முக்கியமான இடங்கள்:

📍 Ho Chi Minh City / Saigon – பரபரப்பான மோட்டார் சைக்கிள்கள், skyscrapers, shopping malls, nightlife மற்றும் modern city life.

🏔️ Sapa – மலைகள், terrace rice fields, குளிர்ச்சியான காலநிலை மற்றும் பழங்குடியின மக்களின் பாரம்பரிய வாழ்க்கை.

🦇 Phong Nha-Ke Bang – பல கோடி ஆண்டுகளாக உருவாகிய limestone karst பாறைகள் மற்றும் பிரம்மாண்டமான குகை உலகம்.

🕳️ Son Doong Cave – உலகின் மிகப்பெரிய குகை அமைப்புகளில் ஒன்றாக புகழ்பெற்ற இயற்கை அதிசயம்.

🏛️ Hanoi – வியட்நாமின் தலைநகர், French architecture, பழமையான கோவில்கள், narrow streets மற்றும் வரலாற்றுச் சின்னங்கள்.

🛕 One Pillar Pagoda – வியட்நாமின் புகழ்பெற்ற பழமையான புத்த மதக் கட்டிடங்களில் ஒன்று.

🍜 Vietnamese Food – Pho, Banh Mi, Spring Rolls, Seafood மற்றும் பல்வேறு street foods.

☕ Vietnamese Coffee – உலகப் புகழ்பெற்ற Robusta coffee, Condensed Milk Coffee மற்றும் Hanoi Egg Coffee.

🌊 Ha Long Bay – கடலுக்கு நடுவே எழுந்து நிற்கும் ஆயிரக்கணக்கான limestone islands மற்றும் breathtaking landscapes.

🌾 Ninh Binh – பசுமையான நெற்பயிர் வயல்கள், ஆறுகள், limestone mountains மற்றும் பழமையான கோவில்களுடன் கூடிய cinematic destination.

🏙️ Landmark 81 – 461.2 மீட்டர் உயரம் கொண்ட வியட்நாமின் பிரபலமான skyscraper.

மேலும் இந்த வீடியோவில் Vietnam War history, Vietnam culture, Tet Festival, Water Puppetry, Non La, Vietnamese currency, Vietnam travel cost, Vietnam trip budget, Vietnam tourism places போன்ற பல சுவாரஸ்யமான தகவல்களையும் தெரிந்துகொள்ளலாம்.

💰 Vietnam Travel Budget:

title: Top 10 Must Try Vietnamese Foods 🇻🇳  || Vietnam Best Street Food & Traditional Dishes!
description:
Top 10 Must Try Vietnamese Foods 🇻🇳  || Vietnam Best Street Food & Traditional Dishes!

Vietnam is a food lover's paradise, offering a diverse culinary experience packed with fresh ingredients, vibrant flavors, and aromatic herbs. From iconic street food to rich traditional dishes, Vietnamese cuisine reflects its deep cultural heritage. Here are the top 10 most popular foods in Vietnam that you must try!
Vietnam is famous for its rich culinary heritage, offering a perfect blend of flavors, textures, and fresh ingredients. From bustling street food stalls to fine dining restaurants, Vietnamese cuisine caters to every taste. In this video, we introduce you to the top 10 most popular Vietnamese dishes that showcase the country’s unique food culture.
One of the most iconic dishes is Pho, a flavorful noodle soup made with beef (Pho Bo) or chicken (Pho Ga). The broth, simmered for hours with bones, star anise, and cinnamon, creates a rich and aromatic flavor. Topped with fresh herbs, lime, and chili, Pho is a must-try dish that represents the soul of Vietnamese cuisine.
Another favorite is Banh Mi, a Vietnamese baguette sandwich that combines crispy French bread with flavorful fillings such as pate, grilled meats, pickled vegetables, and fresh cilantro. A perfect on-the-go meal, Banh Mi showcases the fusion of Vietnamese and French culinary influences.
For a fresh and healthy option, Goi Cuon, or fresh spring rolls, are a great choice. These delicate rice paper rolls are filled with shrimp, pork, vermicelli noodles, and fresh herbs, served with a peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. Light and flavorful, they are a perfect snack or appetizer.
If you’re visiting Hanoi, Bun Cha is a must-try dish. It consists of grilled pork patties and pork belly served with vermicelli noodles, fresh herbs, and a sweet-savory dipping sauce. This dish gained international recognition when former U.S. President Barack Obama enjoyed it during his Vietnam visit.
In Southern Vietnam, Com Tam (broken rice) is a popular dish. Typically served with a grilled pork chop, fried egg, shredded pork skin, and pickled vegetables, it is drizzled with a flavorful fish sauce-based dressing. This simple yet satisfying meal is a staple in Vietnamese cuisine.

title: Hoi An Ancient Town, Vietnam (January 2025)
description:
Hoi An is an ancient town located along the Thu Bon River in central Vietnam, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999. It was a major Southeast Asian trading port from the 15th to the 19th century, where merchants from Japan, China, and Europe exchanged goods such as silk, ceramics, and spices.

The town's architecture is a blend of Vietnamese, Japanese, Chinese, and French influences, preserved in wooden shop houses, tiled roofs, and narrow alleys. The iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, built in the 16th century, symbolizes centuries of cultural exchange. Hoi An's grid-like street plan reflects its historical mercantile function and features over 1,000 timber-framed buildings. 

Seasonal flooding from the Thu Bon River has shaped local building techniques, including elevated floors and flood-adapted storefronts. Traditional crafts like lantern-making, woodcarving, and tailoring continue to thrive, supporting a living heritage economy.

title: Vietnam's 1,500-Year Empire Lost To History: Living Relics Of Champa Kingdom | The Mark Of Empire
description:
Linked to ancient seafarers from Taiwan, the Champa were expert sailors and vital players in global trade. On land, they were skilled builders and innovative agriculturalists who also made their mark on the modern world. Curator and scholar Peter Lee embarks on a quest to uncover the story of the Champa Kingdom and its glory years.

From visiting the ancient, hallowed grounds of My Son Sanctuary where grand temples showcase the king’s authority, to learning about modern Cham identity with a local rap artist, Peter traces the great heights that the kingdom reached before its eventual decline. But in recent years, a new generation of Cham people are striving for pride and recognition of their ancient heritage.

title: Walking Through Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra Peninsula | 4K Silent Walking Tour Da Nang
description:
Walk with me through Linh Ung Pagoda — a sacred temple resting on Son Tra Peninsula, home to Vietnam's tallest Lady Buddha statue, overlooking the entire bay of Da Nang. This video has no narration and no added music — only the real sounds of the mountains: temple bells, wind, and the distant sea.

Linh Ung Pagoda is one of three famous "Linh Ung" temples in Da Nang, built on sacred ground where the Lady Buddha is said to have once appeared. Standing 67 meters tall among the clouds, the statue of Avalokiteshvara (Quan The Am Bo Tat) is one of Da Nang's most iconic landmarks — a place of both worship and quiet reflection.

title: When Is the Best Time to Visit Hoi An Old Town? | Season + Time of Day Explained
description:
When is the best time to visit Hoi An Old Town? The answer depends on more than just the weather.
In this guide, we break down the best time to visit Hoi An Old Town by season and time of day, so you can choose when to visit based on the kind of experience you want.
From February to April, Hoi An generally becomes milder and sunnier, making it comfortable for walking and exploring. May to July brings hotter weather, brighter days, more visitors, and higher accommodation demand around Da Nang's International Fireworks Festival.
August and September are a transition period, with the summer heat gradually easing while rain becomes more important. October and November are the wettest months, with a higher chance of heavy rain and flooding, although rainy season does not mean it rains all day, every day. December and January are generally drier and milder, although the weather can still be changeable.
The video also covers Tet, the Vietnamese Lunar New Year, when Hoi An becomes extremely busy and many businesses may close for several days at the beginning of the new year.
You'll also find a practical breakdown of the best times of day to explore Hoi An Old Town - from the quiet streets of early morning, to the most convenient sightseeing hours, changing afternoon light, and the lantern-filled atmosphere after dark.

title: Hoi An Lantern Festival – Should You Go on Full Moon Night?
description:
Should you go to the Hoi An Lantern Festival on full moon night?
It depends on the kind of experience you're looking for.
The Hoi An Lantern Festival is one of the most beautiful and iconic experiences in Vietnam. Every month, on the 14th day of the lunar calendar, lanterns illuminate the ancient town while parts of the public street lighting are dimmed, creating the warm atmosphere that has made Hoi An famous around the world.
But full-moon night is also the busiest time to visit.
In this video, Discover Da Nang shows you what the Hoi An Lantern Festival is really like during peak hours. We explore the busiest areas of the Ancient Town, including the Night Market, the Japanese Covered Bridge, and the Hoai River, where visitors line up for boat rides and floating lantern experiences.
Rather than simply recommending the festival, this video presents both sides of the experience. You'll see the beauty of thousands of glowing lanterns, but also the reality of large crowds, busy streets, and long queues that many first-time visitors don't expect.
You'll also learn practical tips before visiting, including:
• The best time to experience Hoi An at night
• Where the largest crowds usually gather
• What to expect from boat rides on the Hoai River
• How boat prices are typically arranged
• Tips for avoiding confusion before boarding
• A more environmentally responsible way to enjoy Hoi An's famous floating lantern tradition
If you prefer a quieter atmosphere, we also share some of the best alternatives - including weekday evenings, arriving before the peak crowds, staying later after most visitors leave, and exploring the peaceful streets just beyond the busiest tourist areas.
Whether you're planning your first trip to Hoi An or deciding if full-moon night is right for you, this video offers an honest, balanced look at one of Vietnam's most photographed destinations.

VIETNAM VISA FOR INDIANS (2026)
Mainland Vietnam (Hanoi · Da Nang · Ho Chi Minh) needs an e-visa: USD 25 single-entry / USD 50 multiple-entry, valid up to 90 days.

Apply ONLY on the official portal: https://evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn

THE PHU QUOC VISA-FREE TRAP
Phu Quoc gives Indians a 30-day VISA-FREE stay — but ONLY if you fly in directly from abroad (via Bangkok / Kuala Lumpur) AND it is your only stop in Vietnam. The moment you transit Ho Chi Minh or Hanoi, that visa-free status is VOID and you need the e-visa. Doing a multi-city trip? title: Jeep ride 🚙 through Hai Van pass & Hoi An 🏮 tailored clothes 👗 Ep. 6: Solo Backpacking Vietnam 🇻🇳
description:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to my channel and to episode 6 of my solo female backpacking Vietnam. In this episode we left Hue and got into open-air jeeps! We drove through the stunning landscapes of the Hai Van pass, which divides northern and southern Vietnam. The end of the road trip brought us to Hoi An. This is a popular city for tourists and it is easy to see why. Walking in the old quarter you can marvel at the old architecture and take in the numerous lanterns hanging from above. You're transported back in time to old Vietnam and it's this charm that makes Hoi An a top tourist destination. The other big draw is the custom-made tailored clothing. People travel from around the world to get clothes made by the thousands of tailors you can find here. It felt like there were more tailor shops in Hoi An than lanterns - which is saying something! I definitely indulged and had a couple clothes tailor-made for my measurements - which was pretty awesome. While I did have some unfortunate events happen in Hoi An, and the tour group dynamics were testing my patience - I was able to set all of that aside and celebrate my 31st birthday. The tour guide bought me a cake and it was a special, thoughtful moment during the group dinner. 

Thank you so much for watching and don't forget to subscribe to watch the next episode! We continued travelling down south along the coast. 

Kyra Mioso

-Morning: Start with a sunrise at a stunning beach, known for its soft sand and calm waters. It's the perfect spot for a morning jog or a relaxing swim.
-Afternoon: Head to the Son Tra Peninsula and climb to the magnificent pagoda, home to the towering Lady Buddha statue. The views from the pagoda are absolutely breathtaking!
-Evening: Experience the spectacle of the Dragon Bridge fire and water show, which takes place every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday at 9 PM. Grab dinner at a local seafood spot or explore the vibrant night market nearby.

Day 2: Culture, Comfort & City Sights
-Morning: Take a trip to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, an ancient complex of temples that offers a deep dive into Vietnam's rich history.
-Afternoon: After a day of exploring, unwind with a traditional Vietnamese massage. You deserve it!
-Evening: Enjoy a delicious bowl of a local noodle specialty and explore the city center.

title: DaNang to Hue by Train - Vietnam Railways | Hai Van Pass Train | Danang Travel Guide 3
description:
Join Alex in Vietnam, as he embarks on an unforgettable journey from Danang to Hue aboard the newly inaugurated Connecting Central Heritage Train. This scenic train ride, internationally acclaimed as one of the best in the world, offers breathtaking views of the Hai Van Pass, Lang Co Bay, and the Tam Giang Lagoon System. 

As the Hai Van Pass Train winds through the mountains and along the coastline, you'll experience the stunning natural beauty and cultural richness of Central Vietnam.

[Don't forget to turn on subtitles by clicking on the CC/settings button! 👆]

The Central Heritage Connection, launched on the 49th anniversary of Hue Liberation Day, bridges the heritage cities of Danang and Hue with a picturesque rail route. Enjoy onboard cultural activities and panoramic views, making this a travel experience like no other.

Upon arrival in Hue, I explored the bustling Dong Ba Market. Established in 1899, this market is a historical and cultural hub where you can find everything from daily necessities to unique souvenirs. Wander through its extensive 15,000 square meters, sampling local delicacies and experiencing the vibrant atmosphere.

The adventure continues at Songplatform, a cutting-edge digital art exhibition that brings Hue's rich history to life. Opened in December 2023, this 1,000 square meter space features five themed rooms showcasing innovative digital artworks. From 3D paintings to interactive light mapping, Songplatform offers a mesmerizing blend of tradition and modernity.

Don’t miss this episode of "Alex in Vietnam" as he uncovers the hidden gems and cultural treasures between Danang and Hue.

title: Our Vietnam Travel Guide 2024 | First time in HANOI, HOI AN, & HO CHI MINH
description:
In today's video we visit the amazingly beautiful country of Vietnam and provide travel tips and tricks to make your visit better. Vietnam is a beautiful and culturally rich country that has become a popular destination for travelers from all over the world and 2024 is a great time to visit.

Hanoi, the capital city, is known for its bustling streets, French colonial architecture, and delicious street food. Some of the top attractions in Hanoi include the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Temple of Literature, and the Old Quarter.

Hoi An, located in central Vietnam, is a picturesque city known for its well-preserved Ancient Town, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The town features charming streets lined with historic buildings, temples, and colorful lanterns. Hoi An is also famous for its tailor shops, where visitors can have custom-made clothing and accessories created for them. We visited Hoi An especially for the amazing lantern festival, which is held each month during the full moon.

Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Saigon, is the largest city in Vietnam and is located in the southern part of the country. The city is a vibrant hub of culture and commerce, with numerous markets, museums, and historical sites to explore. Some of the top attractions in Ho Chi Minh City include the War Remnants Museum, the Cu Chi Tunnels, and the Notre-Dame Cathedral.

Traveling from Hanoi to Hoi An and then down to Ho Chi Minh City allows visitors to experience a diverse range of cultural and historical attractions, as well as stunning landscapes and delicious cuisine. The journey between these cities can be made by plane, train, bus, or private car, and there are numerous tour companies and travel agencies that can help plan and organize a trip. We took Vietnam Airlines between locations and everything turned out great.

title: Vietnam’s Most Dangerous Mountain Road, The Hai Van Pass
description:
Week 21 in Da Nang. We'd had our motorbike for exactly two days when we decided to ride it up and over the Hai Van Pass. One of the most iconic mountain roads in Southeast Asia.

Friends visiting from the UK were driving up to Hue, we joined them for the ride over, stopped at a cafe on the way up, had seafood lunch at Lang Co beach, then turned around and rode home alone through the fog.

Got a little damp. Made it back before dark. 10/10 would do again. Genuinely one of the coolest days we've had in Vietnam.

If you're planning to do the Hai Van Pass — do it. Details below.

title: Hue Vietnam 4K | Explore the Imperial City, Royal Tombs & Hương River
description:
Huế, Vietnam 4K — take a quiet journey through Vietnam’s former imperial capital, where ancient architecture, peaceful landscapes and the gentle Hương River create one of the country’s most atmospheric destinations.

This visual journey through Huế, Vietnam invites you to experience the city without narration — only beautiful scenery, gentle music and the quiet atmosphere of each place.

Travel through the historic Imperial City of Huế, admire the restored beauty of Kiến Trung Palace, and wander among the royal landscapes of Minh Mạng Mausoleum and Khải Định Mausoleum. Follow the Hương River past Thiên Mụ Pagoda and Trường Tiền Bridge, then discover the colors of Thủy Xuân Incense Village and the peaceful natural scenery surrounding Huế.

Once the imperial capital of the Nguyễn Dynasty, Huế, Vietnam is a place where architecture, history, nature and a slower rhythm of life still exist side by side.

There is no story to follow in this film and nothing you need to understand.
Just slow down, listen, and spend a little time in Huế.

title: How to Visit Hoi An from Da Nang: Full Travel Guide
description:
How to Visit Hoi An from Da Nang | Complete Travel Guide

Hoi An is just 30km south of Da Nang — around 45 minutes to 1 hour by car. You can take a taxi, book a Grab, ride a shuttle, or take the Yellow Public Bus (cheapest option, but less comfortable).

Many travelers visit Hoi An as a day trip, but staying at least one night is recommended to fully enjoy the atmosphere, food, and lantern-lit streets.

Top Things to Know:

Historical Significance: Hoi An was a major Southeast Asian trading port from the 15th to 19th century. Merchants from China, Japan, and Europe left behind a unique mix of architecture.

UNESCO World Heritage Site: The ancient town is exceptionally well preserved.

Lantern Festival: Held monthly during the full moon. Electric lights are turned off, and the streets glow with lanterns and candles on the river.

Tailor Shops: Over 400 shops offer custom suits, dresses, shoes, and bags — often completed within 1–2 days.

Night Market: Starts around 5 PM across the river. Expect street food, souvenirs, and colorful lanterns.

Local Food to Try:

Cao Lau – chewy noodles with pork, herbs, and croutons
White Rose Dumplings
Hoi An Banh Mi
Cooking Classes: Includes market tours and hands-on instruction.

Travel Tips:

Ask for Grab driver prices upfront to avoid detours or upselling.
Avoid common upsells at tailor shops and souvenir stores.
Morning visits offer fewer crowds and better photo opportunities.
Keep an eye on your belongings at the night market.

This guide gives you everything you need to visit Hoi An with confidence and make the most of your time there.

    Crispy Vietnamese Pancake:
 Ingredients:
 • White rice powder (50g)
 • Water (100ml)
 • Turmeric powder (0.05g)
 • Spring onion (0.05g)
 • Mushroom (10g)
 • Oil
 • Bean sprout
 • Soysauce for dipping
 • Preparation:
 • Mix water, rice powder, turmeric, and spring onion in a large bowl for 5 minutes.
 • Prepare a small bowl of mushroom.
 • Heat a pan and pour some oil.
 • Pour 4 soup spoons of rice powder milk onto the pan.
 • Place some bean sprout, mushroom, and cover for 3 minutes.
 • Serve on a plate with fresh vegetables and soy sauce for dipping.
 Banana Flower Salad:
       Ingredients:
 • Banana flower (0.2kg)
 • Papaya (0.2kg)
 • Boiled bird egg (2)
 • Tofu (0.1kg)
 • Onion (0.05kg)
 • Pepper mint (0.03kg)
 • Dry peanut bean (0.01kg)
 • Sweet and sour fish sauce for mixing salad:
 • Chilli sauce (1 coffee spoon)
 • Lime juice (1 coffee spoon)
 • Fish sauce (2 coffee spoons)
 • Sugar (1 coffee spoon)
 • Method:
 • Heat a pan and stir-fry tofu, black pepper, sugar for 3 minutes.
 • Wait for it to cool.
 • Mix salad with banana flower, papaya, onions, mint, and sauce.
 • Serve on a plate and decorate with sesame, peanut, and boiled egg.
 Grilled Eggplant on Charcoal with Peanut Sauce:
 Ingredients:
 • Peanut sauce:
 • Onion (0.02kg)
 • Shallot (0.02kg)
 • Ginger (0.02kg)
 • Dry peanut (0.02kg)
 • Method:
 • Chop onion, shallot, ginger, and grind dry peanut.
 • Heat a pan and cook the peanut sauce.
 • Grill eggplant on charcoal.
 • Serve with peanut sauce.
 • Heat the pan and add some cooking oil.
 • Pour the marinated vegetables (soya sauce, fish sauce, sugar, black pepper, dry peanut, chilli sauce) into the pan.
 • Cook until the vegetables are fragrant.
 • Pour the mixture into a small bowl.
 • This recipe serves 2 people.
 • Grill the eggplant until well done.
 • Peel the skin and cut the eggplant into small pieces.
 • Take one soup spoon of peanut sauce and pour it over the eggplant.
 • Decorate the plate with the eggplant.
 • Buy fresh rice noodle paper or dry rice paper and dip it in warm water.
 • Take one small spoon of peanut sauce and put it on the rice paper.
 • Roll the rice paper and cut it in half.
 • Decorate the plate with the rice paper.
 Chicken Cao Lau:
 Ingredients:
 • Chicken breast slice: 0.3kg
 • Spring onion chop: 0.01kg
 • Chilli sauce: 1 chilli spoon
 • Soya sauce
 • Cao lau noodle: 0.5kg
 • Bean Sprout: 0.3kg
 • Method:
 • Heat the pan and add some cooking oil.
 • Pour the chicken into the pan and cook for 5 minutes.
 • Stir-fry the Cao lau noodle and try until it’s cooked.
 • Add chilli sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and stir-fry everything together with the spring onion.
 • Pour the mixture into a bowl and decorate with black pepper.
 Caramel Banana:
 • Heat the pan until it’s really hot.
 • Pour some sugar into the pan.
 • Put the fresh banana on the pan.
 • Cook for 2 minutes, then turn the banana over.
 • Pick up the plate and serve.

title: Exploring a Serene Mountain Temple with a Hidden Sacred Cave: Quan The Am Pagoda | Walking Tour [4K]
description:
Take an immersive 4K walking tour through Quan The Am Pagoda, a peaceful Buddhist temple at the foot of the Marble Mountains in Da Nang, Vietnam. Surrounded by towering limestone cliffs and tropical greenery, this remarkable place offers a quiet escape from the busy city — along with a mysterious cave hidden deep within the mountain.

Follow our silent guide as she explores remarkable places around the world — no talking, no music, only real sounds.

Located near the famous Marble Mountains, Quan The Am Pagoda is dedicated to Quan Am, the Bodhisattva of Compassion, known in many Buddhist traditions as Avalokiteshvara. The temple is a place of worship and reflection, where traditional Vietnamese Buddhist architecture blends with the dramatic natural landscape.

As we explore the temple grounds, we'll discover peaceful courtyards, Buddhist statues, colorful architectural details, and beautiful views of the surrounding mountains. The towering rock formations provide an extraordinary backdrop, making the entire setting feel far removed from the streets of Da Nang.

But there's more to discover beyond the temple itself.

Hidden within the limestone mountain is Quan Am Cave (Động Quan Âm), a fascinating underground sanctuary where natural rock formations and Buddhist religious traditions come together. Inside, narrow passages lead deeper into the mountain, while carefully placed lighting reveals the unusual shapes and textures of the cave walls.

The atmosphere changes as we move from the open temple grounds into the enclosed spaces of the cave. The light becomes softer, the outside world feels more distant, and the mountain reveals an entirely different side of itself.

What makes this place so memorable is the contrast between its peaceful temple courtyards and the mysterious world hidden inside the rock. It's a reminder that some of the most interesting places around Da Nang are found just beyond the city's busy streets.

There is no narration and no added background music — only authentic stereo recordings of footsteps, distant voices, birds, and the natural sounds of the temple grounds and cave, captured as we experienced them.

🎧 For the best immersive experience, use headphones.

Vietnam Itinerary 10 days - 8 Cities Tour North to South of Vietnam
Hanoi - 4 Days (with Halong Bay & Ninh Binh)

PHU QUOC DUONG DONG RESORT - https://tripadvisor.tpk.ro/VvmyM59V
HO CHI MINH CITY
**********************************************************************
FOOD TIPS 
For Vietnamese Vegetarian Food, search for the Met Vietnamese chain of restaurants. They have vegetarian fried rice, many vegetarian curries, vegetarian noodles, and many more vegetarian options. 
Must-Try Drinks:
 ☕ Coconut Cream Vietnamese Coffee
 🥭 Passion Fruit Juice
 ☕ Condensed Milk Vietnamese Coffee (Hot or Iced) — rich, sweet, and creamy, an absolute must!
Day 1: Explore Hanoi Old Quarter with the famous train street tour. You arrive late morning, so explore the Old Quarter, Lakeside Temple, the French Quarter & evening nightlife at Famous Train Street with a Vietnamese lunch and an *******Indian Dinner at Indian Masala in the Old Quarter*************.
Day 2: Book a long trip to Halong Bay with lunch and evening snacks/tea. This cruise stops at 4 to 5 places with lots of activities.
Day 3 - Again, book a long day trip to Ninh Binh, which has 3 excellent stops -Hoa Lu: Explore the ancient temples of Dinh King and Le King, the historic capital of Vietnam in the 10th and 11th centuries. Bike across the countryside of Vietnam, and this biking is included in your day trip.
Trang An Grottoes (or Tam Coc): Take a scenic boat tour through a UNESCO World Heritage site, navigating through caves and lush landscapes. 
Mua Caves: Hike up approximately 500 steps to the Ngoa Long mountain viewpoint for impressive panoramic views of Ninh Binh.  Or explore the Lotus garden/pond below.
Day 4: Early morning, explore Hanoi shopping with a great body massage. Fly to Danang via Viet Jet.
If you arrive late in Danang, have dinner at Bhojan Indian restaurant near Danang beach, as our hotel is located there on the beachside. 
Protip: Vietjet gets delayed many times, so keep a margin for the next flight or keep yourself free after that so that some activities don't overlap.
Day 5: Book the Bana Hills full-day Cable ride tour with buffet lunch. An excellent theme park and the longest cable ride in the world, famous in the Guinness World Records. As our Day 4 was wasted in the flight delay, we combined Hoi An on the same day. After Bana Hills, visit Coconut village with a unique rotating basket boat ride across coconut trees in the lagoons. After that, visit Hoi An and do a Lantern boat ride. Hoi is famous as the Lantern City of Vietnam. Explore this city on foot, where you can find amazing lanterns, Vietnamese-style cafes, bars, shopping, silk, tailoring, and much more to do till late at night. Return late to Danang. Our hotel in Danag was on Danag beach.
Day 6: Explore Danang beaches and nearby beaches, and drive to Hue city, approximately 180 km from Danang. In between, you stop at many beautiful spots. Hue City is a historical city with a tomb and a Citadel.
Day 7: Early morning checkout and fly to Phu Quoc Island via Vietnam Airlines. Check into a resort-style island vibes hotel. After that, book a 4-island-hopping speedboat tour with sunset from the boat. You can also watch the sunset with a special show from Sunset Village.
Have an **Indian dinner at Ganesh Indian restaurant*** in the main Duong Dong market. 
Day 8: Visit Grand World - an Italy-style town in Phu Quoc with many colorful streets, shopping, and beaches. Fly on Day 8 to Ho Chi Minh City and check into a hotel at the city centre near Saigon Square late in the evening.
Day 9: Book a half-day trip to cu Chi tunnels to know about the American-Vietnamese War. After having lunch on tour, return and explore the walking markets of Ho Chi Minh City, which are famous for shopping.
Then explore the famous nightlife of Ho Chi Minh City at Bui Vien 
Street for a wild night out. For an *******Indian vegetarian restaurant, have food at the Gujarat Indian restaurant******** at Saiqon Square of Grand Market. 
******************************************
Markets in Ho Chi Minh City
1. Ben Tahn Market

3. Taka underground market
4. Biu Vien walking street for cabaret and bars

title: Golden Bridge Vietnam: Is Ba Na Hills Worth $39? Real Costs to Know Before You Go (2026)
description:
Is Ba Na Hills worth it? In about 8 minutes, here is the honest answer before you go: the record-breaking Toc Tien cable car, the Golden Bridge and its crowds, the French Village and Fantasy Park (what your ticket covers and what costs extra), the real total cost of a day trip from Da Nang, and 3 rules to get your money's worth, with real prices in US dollars on screen.

Short version: the Golden Bridge is a theme park in the clouds, not an ancient wonder. Catch the very first cable car of the day, watch the weather from September to December, and a day at Ba Na Hills turns from a tourist trap into a genuinely fun day out.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Is it worth it? (intro)
1:08 The record-breaking cable car
2:09 The Golden Bridge (and the crowds)
3:26 French Village & Fantasy Park: what's included
4:39 The real cost: ticket, transport & buffet
6:05 3 rules: weather, 3-day ticket, what to wear
7:09 Verdict: who should go (and who shouldn't)

REAL PRICES (approx., converted at 1 USD ≈ 25,500 VND)
- Cable car ticket, adult (non-Da Nang resident): about $39
- Kids 1–1.4 m and seniors 70+: about $31 · kids under 1 m: free
- Ticket + lunch buffet combo: about $50
- Alpine Coaster: about $3 per ride · Wax museum: about $4
- Grab car, central Da Nang to Ba Na Hills (25–30 km, 45–60 min): about $12–18 each way
- Rough estimate, one adult, one day: $75–90 (ticket + buffet, car both ways, a coaster ride and a drink)
- Since January 2026 the cable car ticket is valid for 3 consecutive days (unlimited rides for 72 hours). Confirm when you buy.

Prices, opening hours and ticket rules change often. Please check the official Sun World website before you book. Fog and drizzle are common from September to December; check the summit forecast the morning you go.

Not into theme parks? Son Tra Peninsula and the Marble Mountains are in our Da Nang travel guide. If this Ba Na Hills guide helped you plan your trip, like and subscribe for the full Vietnam series.

title: I TRIED A VIETNAMESE COOKING CLASS! Come cook with me in Hoi An! (+ Coconut Baskets!)
description:
Cooking Class & Coconut Basket Boats 🌿🇻🇳 | A Day in Hoi An, Vietnam

Welcome to Hoi An! After the slightly traumatic motorbike ride getting here, we decided to slow things down with a day of food, culture, and a little bit of fun on the river.

✨ Vietnamese Cooking Class
We signed up for an authentic cooking class through our lovely hostel, Riverside Hoi An Dolphin Hostel. You can choose between a morning session (cooking lunch) or an afternoon session (cooking dinner). We went for the morning option to make the most of the day!

The experience began with a stroll through a local food market, where our wonderful teacher Lily introduced us to fresh herbs, fruit, and vegetables before taking us to the kitchen.

✨ Viral Coconut Basket Boats
Before cooking, we hopped into the famous coconut basket boats,the round boats you’ve probably seen all over Instagram! The ride itself was included in the price, but we paid a little extra to try the spinning version (which was so much fun). Shoutout to the guy blasting Gangnam Style while rowing, it definitely added to the vibes!

✨ What We Cooked
Back at the kitchen, we prepared a full Vietnamese feast:
🥟 Fresh spring rolls
🥗 Papaya salad
🥘 Clay pot dishes (the aubergine was divine!)
🥞 Vietnamese pancakes (complete with flambé!)

The boys went for chicken, pork, and fish options, while I stuck with my new vegetarian diet. Honestly, every dish was delicious and cooking it ourselves made it even better.

This was such a fun and memorable experience, we’d highly recommend a cooking class if you’re in Hoi An.

Hope you enjoy the vlog 💛 Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more Vietnam adventures!
